test_title: PYST 50 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 30 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. He presented his diagnosis and suggested a course of treatment with assurance.

Q. In order to search for particular markers, he ordered a number of imaging scans and blood tests.

R. He went over all the information, comparing it to what he knew about medicine.

S. As the patient explained their symptoms, the doctor paid close attention.
solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. S, Q, R, P .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph, the sentence parts need to be arranged in a logical sequence based on the progression of ideas.
 
• The sequence should follow the natural flow of events or actions described.
 
• Each part contributes to the narrative, starting with the introduction of the situation and progressing to the resolution or conclusion.

Correct arrangement:

 
• **S:** As the patient explained their symptoms, the doctor paid close attention.
 
• **Q:** In order to search for particular markers, he ordered a number of imaging scans and blood tests.
 
• **R:** He went over all the information, comparing it to what he knew about medicine.
 
• **P:** He presented his diagnosis and suggested a course of treatment with assurance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The sequence starts with the doctor listening to the patient’s explanation (**S**).
 
• It then progresses to the doctor’s actions to investigate the issue further by ordering tests (**Q**).
 
• After gathering the necessary information, the doctor analyzes and compares it to his knowledge (**R**).
 
• Finally, the doctor provides a diagnosis and suggests a treatment plan (**P**).
